explain.say: In 1516 Thomas More invented a word for a perfect island society: utopia, a Greek pun meaning both good place and no place. Dystopian fiction imagines the opposite, a society gone horribly wrong, usually to warn us about our own. The timeline runs from More to novels written in your lifetime.

explain.say: Listen to the word itself. Dys is Greek for bad, top means place, as in topography, and ia makes it a noun: a bad place. The philosopher John Stuart Mill used an early form of the word in a speech to Parliament in 1868. What is the worst place you can imagine, and what would it warn against?

draw.note: dys bad + topos place: a bad place

explain.say: Two classics, two kinds of control. On the left, Orwell's 1949 novel: Big Brother watches everyone, history is rewritten, and Newspeak, a shrinking language, makes rebellious thought impossible. On the right, Huxley's 1932 novel, where people are bred in labs and kept content with a drug called soma. Which nightmare is closer to our world: fear or pleasure?

In Margaret Atwood's 1985 novel The Handmaid's Tale, a religious regime called Gilead has taken over part of the United States and forces fertile women, the Handmaids, to bear children for powerful men. Atwood has said she included nothing that humans had not already done somewhere in history. Why would that rule make it more frightening?

explain.say: Sort the toolkit most dystopias share: surveillance and propaganda, a hero who starts to doubt, a forbidden love, and an ending that crushes hope or leaves it open. Both Orwell and Atwood end with notes written from a later time, hinting that the regime fell. Superb. Challenge: invent a dystopia from one trend you see today, and give it a slogan.

faq.a: An imagined society that is frightening or oppressive, often presented as ideal by its rulers. Dystopian fiction exaggerates real trends, such as surveillance or control of bodies, to warn readers.

faq.q: What is the difference between utopia and dystopia?
faq.a: A utopia is an imagined perfect society, from Thomas More's 1516 book; the word puns on Greek for good place and no place. A dystopia is its nightmare opposite, a bad place.

faq.q: What is the difference between Nineteen Eighty-Four and Brave New World?
faq.a: Orwell's regime controls people through fear, surveillance, torture and language. Huxley's controls them through pleasure, conditioning and drugs, so that people love their servitude and do not want to rebel.
The face of the Party in Nineteen Eighty-Four, seen on posters everywhere with the warning that he is watching you. He may not exist as a person; he is the image of total surveillance.
asks: Big Brother is watching you meaning

faq.q: Why did Atwood say nothing in The Handmaid's Tale was invented?
faq.a: Atwood set herself the rule of including only things people had already done somewhere, such as controlling women's reproduction, banning reading or public executions, so readers could not dismiss Gilead as impossible.
asks: Is The Handmaid's Tale based on real events?

facts: Thomas More's Utopia was published in 1516.
Nineteen Eighty-Four was published in June 1949, seven months before Orwell's death.
Atwood's sequel The Testaments shared the Booker Prize in 2019.
